Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP View image in fullscreen Former radio broadcaster Alan Jones leaves the Downing Centre local court in Sydney on Tuesday. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP Alan Jones trial Alan Jones and fellow 2GB host referred to SMH and reporter as ‘pigs in the media’, court hears Jason Morrison, a former presenter at the Sydney radio station, denies ‘tailoring his evidence’ during trial of veteran shock jock Jones Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Amanda Meade Media correspondent Tue 25 Aug 2026 03.46 EDT Last modified on Tue 25 Aug 2026 04.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Alan Jones and fellow 2GB shock jock Jason Morrison often referred to the Sydney Morning Herald and its chief investigative reporter Kate McClymont as “pigs in the media”, a Sydney court has heard. The text messages were uncovered as Morrison faced accusations from the prosecution on Tuesday of “tailoring his evidence” about an alleged assault at a lower north shore restaurant to suit his friend Jones. Judge Glenn Walsh, who earlier ruled in favour of a prosecution application to cross-examine Morrison, said the crown had tendered evidence that Morrison sent “text messages where clearly he does refer to [the SMH and McClymont] as pigs”. Police said they formed Strike Force Bonnefin, leading to Jones’s trial, after reporting in the Sydney Morning Herald and the Age in 2023 resulted in alleged victims coming forward. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Jones was arrested in November 2024. He has pleaded not guilty to 20 charges of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching against six complainants. On Tuesday, prosecutor Georgina Wright read out a text message that Morrison, a former host at 2GB, sent to Jones in 2020 when he announced his retirement from the Sydney radio station, then owned by the Herald publisher Nine Entertainment (formerly Fairfax). “Thank Christ you’re getting out [of Nine Entertainment]. Let them fall into a bag of shit,” Morrison said to Jones. Wright asked: “You’ve expressed that disdain for both Ms McClymont and the Herald to the defendant. You agree with that?” Morrison said he and Jones “spoke extensively about a lot of things on text” and agreed he had been critical of both the Herald and McClymont. “Well, you’ve referred to Ms McClymont, and at that time Fairfax, as pigs in the media. You agree with that?” asked Wright. Morrison replied: “That’s a phrase Alan used to use a lot.” Morrison said he wasn’t a fan of McClymont’s reporting on the NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption and was “disappointed” that despite speaking on the record at length with her about Jones, she had not included any of his remarks in the article. Morrison agreed he had a “longstanding pejorative view of the Sydney Morning Herald”. ‘Tailored’ evidence Morrison was accused by the prosecution on Tuesday of “tailoring” his evidence about an alleged assault at a lower north shore restaurant to suit his friend Jones. The alleged victim of the assault, known as complainant C, earlier told the court that his much older boss, Jones, had instructed him to sit next to him and then spent the entire lunch with his left hand under the table and either on his leg or on his penis over his pants. Morrison is the third witness to be called to give evidence about the lunch so far, in addition to the complainant, who was a young man in his 20s when he worked for Jones. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion 25:38 Alan Jones on Trial: alleged victim tells court he was 'groomed for 10 years' | Week 3 Morrison told the court on Monday that he had joked with other diners that Jones and C looked “like a great couple” but denied he heard anything about Jones touching C inappropriately. On Tuesday, he denied seeing Jones’s hand under the table. “I mean, if I was aware of that and given … my forthright manner, I would have raised it,” Morrison said. “I didn’t because I didn’t see it.” Wright asked: “Did you hear anyone say to [C] ‘you copped a feel under the table, didn’t you’?” Morrison replied: “I didn’t hear that.” C has told the court that Morrison was party to a conversation after the lunch when it was said C had “copped a feel” under the table . Morrison said there was “lighthearted banter” about Jones and C because Jones had his arm around C’s shoulder but denied seeing anything “romantic” or “sexual” between the two men. Wright asked: “And you’ve tailored your evidence about there being lighthearted banter to assist the defendant, haven’t you?” Morrison replied: “Well that’s offensive. I’m here under oath, and I find that offensive.” Wright suggested Morrison was being “deliberately evasive, in answering those questions about any jokes in [C’s] presence in relation to Alan” and that “merely being stuck with Jones at the table” was not a reason to joke about them being a couple. Morrison denied being evasive and said it “was lighthearted banter that was never met with any intention or malice”. The trial continues. https://www.politico.eu/article/asylum-a.text: BRUSSELS — The number of people claiming asylum in EU countries has fallen sharply, new figures show, with some capitals recording historic lows as tough new rules come into effect. The European Union Agency for Asylum, which oversees operational support for refugees across the bloc, will on Thursday publish data showing 332,000 applications were lodged in EU and Schengen zone countries in the first half of this year — a 17% reduction compared to 2025. “The numbers speak for themselves: Europe’s new migration policy is delivering results. We need to continue to step up our efforts at Europe’s borders,” EU Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner said. Advertisement Advertisement The EU earlier this year agreed on wide-ranging new rules allowing countries to establish “return hubs” in third countries like Albania and Rwanda, to which unsuccessful asylum seekers and other failed migrants can be sent to. It has also drawn up lists of safe countries from which would-be refugees are unlikely to be accepted apart from in exceptional cases. With far-right parties gaining in the polls ahead of key elections in France, Germany, Italy and other EU countries, governments are pushing Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to use her State of the Union speech next week to demonstrate mainstream politicians can take effective action to address concerns about migration . Germany, which is among the countries pushing for more powers to remove failed asylum seekers, saw applications fall by 50% year-on-year. Nonetheless, the anti-immigrant, far-right Alternative for Germany party continues to enjoy electoral success . Sweden recorded just 8,485 applications last year, the lowest level in 40 years, while Denmark — one of the EU’s staunchest opponents of unregulated migration — had registered a historic low of 1,835 applications by the end of November. Austria saw the fewest applications in 23 years and has returned more failed asylum seekers than the number of new ones arriving. At the same time, the statistics show, illegal border crossings have fallen by 55% in the past two years, with Brussels having struck agreements with neighboring countries like Turkey and Serbia to reduce irregular migration.

https://telex.hu/techtud/2026/10/14/yand.text: Menü Kereső Valószínűleg csak vágyálom, hogy egy jól célzott dróntámadás kiütötte az orosz bothadsereget Techtud Legfontosabb Füst gomolyog a Yandex szaszovói központjából az ukrán dróntámadást követően – Forrás: Reuters Világi Máté Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Ukrajna egy ideje támadásokat indít oroszországi raktárak és adatközpontok ellen, hogy ezzel gyengítse Putyin hátországának morálját, és üzenjen a nagyvállalatoknak, hogy nem érdemes támogatni az orosz vezetés háborús vágyait. Október elején például a Yandex szaszovói adatközpontjait érte dróntámadás, ami erős csapás volt az orosz netes infrastruktúrára. A Yandex nagyon hasonlít a Google-re: van keresője, böngészője, illetve kajarendelős és fintechszolgáltatásokat is nyújt. A támadás után azonban úgy tűnhetett, hogy a csapás nemcsak az oroszországi hétköznapi élet megszokott elemeit ütötte ki, hanem az interneten állomásozó orosz bothadsereget is. A közösségi oldalakon sorra jöttek az elemzések , hogy visszaesett az AfD vagy a Reform UK netes támogatói aktivitása, utalva arra, hogy a legtöbb szélsőjobboldali kommentelő valójában széthúzást szító orosz bot volt, és ezek mind a Yandex lebombázott raktárának szerverein laktak. Még Volodimir Zelenszkij is ezt állította . Ahogy azonban az az IT-val általában lenni szokott, a helyzet nem ilyen egyértelmű. Ahogy a felhő nem azt jelenti, hogy az adataink a fejünk felett, egy láthatatlan masszában lebegnek, hanem azt, hogy szerverek tízezrein ülnek szerte a világban, úgy egy nagy zuhanást mutató grafikon sem feltétlenül azt jelenti, amit sokan szeretnének belelátni. A legtöbben a Cloudflare grafikonjára mutogattak, amin az látható, hogy a Yandex adatközpontjait ért találat után 99 százalékkal esett a cég felől érkező orosz forgalom: A Cloudflare Radar oldalán látható, hogy a forgalom 99,6 százaléka bot, és csak 0,4 százaléka valós ember. Ez azonban nem feltétlenül azt jelenti, hogy csak dezinformációt terjesztő botokat érintett a leállás. A grafikonon látható, hogy ez csak a Yandex AS13238 nevű hálózatáról érkező HTTP-lekérések bezuhanását mutatja, tehát nem látni , mennyivel kevesebb poszt vagy komment érkezett orosz területről. Az automatizált botok rengeteg mindent csinálnak a neten, a crawlerek például a keresők indexálásában is részt vesznek, azaz folyamatosan túrják a netet új információk után, hogy a kereső hatékonyabb legyen. Ez persze nem a Yandex sajátossága, a Google, a Bing és igazából minden keresőmotor használ crawlereket, hogy friss maradjon. A Yandex saját botbemutatója alapján az AS13238 nevű hálózatán a weboldalakat átnéző YandexBot működik, tehát a jelenleg rendelkezésre álló adatokból nem lehet leszűrni, hogy a lehaló botok a híreket olvasgatták, vagy a Kreml érdekeit szolgálták MAGA-sapkában, Szent György-kereszttel. Ettől függetlenül tele van most a net anekdotikus bizonyítékokkal arra, hogy csökkent az orosz trollok aktivitása. Ez egyáltalán nincs kizárva, de nincs elég információ ahhoz, hogy ki lehessen jelenteni, hogy Ukrajna komoly csapást mért az orosz dezinformációs bothadseregre. A Yandex két szuperszámítógépe a szaszovói adatközpontban lakik, így akár csak egy áramkimaradás is jelentős gondot okozhat a bothadseregnek, hiszen a YandexGPT és a felhőalapú fordítók leállása megakaszthatja a többnyelvű, gyors posztolást, kommentelést. Emellett persze bizonyos értelemben a crawlerek kiütése is megakasztja a propaganda terjesztését, mert amíg a Yandex nem tudja, mivel frissültek a Kreml-párti híroldalak, nem tudja besorolni azokat, így az oldalak nehezebben jutnak el a felhasználókhoz. Tehát az ukrán dróntámadás a jelenleg rendelkezésre álló adatok szerint valószínűleg a hátországbeli életet nehezítette meg, és nem tűntek el a nyugati országok választásait befolyásolni igyekvő botok. https://vietnam.vnanet.vn/english/tin-va.text: In the News NA Vice President proposes priorities for inter-parliamentary cooperation 08/10/2026 NA Vice President Nguyen Hong Dien addressed the high-level General Debate of the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU-153) in Arusha, Tanzania. National Assembly (NA) Vice President Nguyen Hong Dien delivers a speech at the high-level General Debate of the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU-153). Photo: VNA National Assembly (NA) Vice President Nguyen Hong Dien proposed three priorities for inter-parliamentary cooperation to promote public participation in governance, narrow the gap between commitments and results, and ensure that science and technology serves people while addressing the high-level General Debate of the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU-153) in Arusha, Tanzania, on October 7. Highlighting inclusiveness, trust and opportunities for all as the core foundations of effective governance, Dien affirmed that placing the people at the centre and making them the driving force behind all decisions and actions has helped Vietnam achieve important socio-economic achievements after 40 years of Doi moi (Renewal), while continuing to pursue national development goals in the new era. Vietnam is determined to undertake strong institutional reforms to create a development-enabling environment, with science and technology, innovation, digital transformation, green transition and the circular economy serving as key drivers. The Vietnamese NA is also stepping up lawmaking, supreme oversight and making decisions on major national issues. Against this backdrop, the NA Vice President proposed three priorities for inter-parliamentary cooperation in the coming period: promoting public participation in governance; strengthening oversight, transparency and accountability to narrow the gap between commitments and results; and ensuring that science and technology serve people and help narrow development gaps. Affirming that Vietnam will remain an active and responsible member of the IPU, he stressed the need to turn differences into a basis for dialogue, use dialogue to build and strengthen trust, and turn trust into opportunities and conditions for cooperation and shared development. On the sidelines of IPU-153, Dien met with Speaker of the Tanzanian National Assembly Mussa Azzan Zungu, Speaker of the Azerbaijani National Assembly Sahiba Gafarova, Polish Senator Gabriela Morawa-Stanecka and Canadian MP Robert Oliphant. At his meeting with the Speaker of the Tanzanian National Assembly, Dien conveyed National Assembly President Tran Thanh Man’s greetings and invitation to visit Vietnam to the Tanzanian speaker, and affirmed that Vietnam attaches importance to its traditional friendship with Tanzania and appreciates the latter’s support for Vietnam’s past struggle for national independence. Vietnam wishes to further deepen and expand bilateral relations in a more effective manner, he said. To enhance bilateral cooperation, Dien proposed stepping up high-level delegation exchanges through Party, parliamentary and government channels, as well as people-to-people exchanges; increasing contacts and sharing legislative experience between specialised committees and lawmakers of the two countries; and considering the signing of a memorandum of understanding on cooperation between the two legislatures. The two sides should also coordinate in promoting negotiations and signing key agreements, including a double taxation avoidance agreement and an agreement on investment promotion and protection, he said. Regarding economic cooperation, Dien noted that bilateral economic ties have made positive progress but remain below their potential. He asked Tanzania to support and facilitate greater participation by Vietnamese businesses, including Viettel’s telecom joint venture Halotel, in telecommunications, infrastructure, digital transformation and e-government projects in Tanzania. A stable and open legal environment is essential for businesses from both countries to expand trade and investment cooperation in promising areas such as mining, energy, high-tech agriculture and infrastructure development, he stressed. Mussa Azzan Zungu praised Vietnam’s socio-economic achievements after 40 years of Doi moi, describing them as a model for Tanzania to study in implementing its “Tanzania Development Vision 2050”. He affirmed that the Tanzanian National Assembly will work to further strengthen its traditional friendship with Vietnam and that the two legislatures should play a greater role in completing the legal framework and overseeing the implementation of cooperation agreements. Speaking highly of Halotel’s operations, the Tanzanian Speaker welcomed continued investment by Vietnamese businesses in agriculture, tourism, mining, technology and infrastructure development. At his meeting with Azerbaijani Speaker Sahiba Gafarova, the two sides discussed bilateral relations and cooperation at parliamentary forums. Gafarova expressed her delight at the elevation of Vietnam-Azerbaijan relations to a Strategic Partnership during General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee To Lam’s visit to Azerbaijan in May 2025. She also sought Vietnam’s support for her candidacy for IPU President for the 2026-2029 term. Dien spoke highly of her candidacy and leadership capabilities and invited Gafarova and other leaders of the Azerbaijani parliament to visit Vietnam at an early date. At his meeting with Polish Senator Gabriela Morawa-Stanecka, Vice President of the IPU, the two sides agreed to promote high-level delegation exchanges, implement the Strategic Partnership framework and strengthen economic and trade cooperation. Morawa-Stanecka described Vietnam as Poland’s largest economic and trade partner in Southeast Asia, highlighting the role of the Vietnamese community in Poland and expressing a desire to expand relations with the region through Vietnam. Dien proposed that the two sides coordinate closely in preparing high-level visits, increase exchanges among parliamentarians, particularly female and young lawmakers, and promote economic, trade and investment cooperation through the implementation of the EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA) and the early ratification of the investment protection agreement. He also asked Poland to encourage other EU member states to support the removal of the “yellow card” warning on Vietnamese seafood and avoid excessive use of trade defence measures. At his meeting with Canadian MP Robert Oliphant, the two sides welcomed positive developments in Vietnam-Canada relations, particularly the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership. Oliphant said that Vietnam is an important partner in Canada’s Indo-Pacific Strategy and a promising market for trade cooperation. He expressed his readiness to promote cooperation in areas where Canada has strengths, including energy, the environment, agriculture, technology, metallurgy and minerals. Dien said the two economies are complementary and have considerable room to expand trade and investment cooperation. He called on the two legislatures to strengthen oversight of the implementation of bilateral agreements and commitments, and promote negotiations to upgrade the current trade framework and conclude an investment protection agreement. The two sides agreed to increase high-level delegation exchanges and contacts between committees, friendship parliamentary groups, young and female lawmakers and local representatives, while continuing to support the Vietnamese community in Canada in playing its role as a bridge between the two countries./.
